result.title: Fast and Accurate Hand Estimation in Pixels, Interaction and World Space
result.comment: 10 pages of main text plus 15 pages of supplementary material; 5 figures; 12 tables; code available at https://github.com/noahcao/FAH
result.summary: Monocular hand mesh estimators commonly predict rig parameters and project the mesh to obtain 2D keypoints. We find that directly predicted 3D joints agree better with 2D predictions, and fitting a mesh to predicted points reduces mesh error. We present FAH (Fast and Accurate Hand Estimation), a family of models built on SAM 3D Body's hand branch through fine-tuning and feature distillation. The models predict corresponding 2D and 3D joints and surface points, fit MANO or MHR-Hand, and optionally estimate anatomical parts and contact without object geometry at inference. Causal refinement reduces acceleration error, and camera estimation places the hands in world space. Experiments show improvements in image-space alignment, hand geometry, contact estimation and world-space tracking over the evaluated baselines. The default ViT-L model runs at 65 fps with mesh fitting on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, or 49 fps with parts and contact enabled. The smallest ViT-S model reaches 125 fps without mesh fitting, parts or contact. Code: https://github.com/noahcao/FAH.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 FAH 系列单目手部网格估计模型：通过微调与特征蒸馏复用 SAM 3D Body 的手部分支，同时预测 2D/3D 关节点与表面点并拟合 MANO/MHR-Hand，可选估计部位与接触，并用因果细化与时序相机估计提升精度与世界坐标跟踪。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文直接预测 3D 关节点而非由网格投影、再以预测点反向拟合网格，以及时序因果细化状态的做法，可能为 LVR 中几何细节是否保留在内部表示、以及 latent 状态如何迭代更新的监督设计提供可供核查的旁证，但与其推理主线无直接关联。
